subject: Structured streams integration playbook - HealthSync
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@healthsync.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: integration@healthsync.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stream + tools enablement — initial details

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We are ready to start the enablement for HealthSync's real-time clinician alerting pipeline. High level: we need streaming outputs for triage messages, function/tool calling to trigger downstream workflows, and strongly typed JSON outputs for ingestion into our analytics layer.

Attached is a first-pass schema export (healthsync-stream-schema-v1.json) and a short notes doc describing sequence length expectations and sample batches. A few constraints to flag up front:
- max tokens per user message ~1,200
- expect frequent short messages (~300–500 tokens) and occasional long batches (~5–7k tokens)
- strict field typing required for post-processing (timestamp iso8601, patient_id string, score float)

Can we do a two-hour working session next week to align on schema evolution, tool-call contract, and runtime tests? Prefer Wed/Thu mornings PST.

Thanks,
Samir
Customer Engineering Lead
HealthSync

Attachments: healthsync-stream-schema-v1.json (application/json)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@healthsync.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stream + tools enablement — initial details

Samir — great to see the schema, thanks for sending. Monica and Marcus are the engineers who will own the runtime integration and schema validation tests on our side.

Proposed next steps before the working session:
1) Pre-call workbook: please complete the attached Feature-Enablement-Workbook.xlsx with 2–3 representative payloads and one end-to-end success/failure example (we included sample rows).
2) Pre-flight questions: share any SOC2/audit constraints or PII handling notes specific to this workflow so we can scope the private-routing options.
3) Call scheduling: Wed 2028-07-18 09:00 PT / Thu 2028-07-19 09:00 PT both work for us — pick one and I’ll send a calendar invite.

I'll prepare a short runbook and an enablement checklist (we'll attach before the session) that covers: schema alignment, function/tool contract (names, inputs, outputs, error semantics), sample streaming config, and performance test plan.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0126

Attachment: Feature-Enablement-Workbook.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Samir Patel <samir@healthsync.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stream + tools enablement — initial details

Thanks Priya — we'll fill out the workbook and confirm Wed 2028-07-18 09:00 PT.
Couple items to flag for the session so you can prep:
- We use strict schema validation in downstream ETL; any extra fields must be namespaced (healthsync_*).
- Tool-calls will need an idempotency key; if the same function call is replayed within 30s, downstream must ignore duplicate.
- Security ask: we'd like a short doc on how Redwood manages ephemeral KV cache and whether any customer tokens are logged. If you can have something ready or a pointer to existing SOC2 artifacts, that would help the audit team.

Samir
